title: A Scholarship for the Mixtape
premise: Seventeen-year-old Silas Halloran has spent years being the responsible one: cooking, budgeting, and holding her three younger siblings together while their mom works hospital night shifts. When she finds cryptic instructions in grandma's recipe box — not for food, but for a long-lost family tradition of 'kitchen symphonies,' mixtapes of songs and recipes meant to be performed at the county's obscure Harvest Table Championship — she realizes the prize money could finally give her family breathing room. But entering means stepping into the spotlight she's spent a lifetime avoiding, and competing against Theo Marchetti, the charming rival who keeps seeing straight through her 'everything is fine' armor. As mom's shifts stretch longer and the family frays, Silas must choose between the safe invisibility that's kept them afloat and the risky, loud, messy act of letting people in — winning not just the championship, but a new definition of family along the way.
about_author: Quentin Brightwater is the pen name of a former line cook who swears the best stories are overheard in dish pits and diner booths at 2 a.m. They write young adult novels about kids who hold families together and deserve to be held, too.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (A Running Total)
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A Tuesday in the Halloran household: burnt grilled cheese, a lost permission slip, mom's 11 p.m. goodbye kiss smelling of hand sanitizer. Silas runs the house like a quiet machine and insists to everyone — including herself — that it's all under control. Emotional beat: loving exhaustion disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box Doesn't Lie
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Hunting for grandma's cornbread card, Silas finds an index card reading 'Track One: flour, salt, memory' with a cassette labeled FOR WHEN IT GETS LOUD. Her little brother Dee plays the tape; it's grandma's voice singing over kitchen sounds. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Rules of the Harvest Table
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Researching at the library, she learns about the defunct Harvest Table Championship — part cook-off, part performance — and its vanished cash endowment, still legally payable if someone completes grandma's tape series. First obstacle: entry requires a 'household ensemble.' She has exactly that, if they'll do it. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an intruder.

chapters.title: Auditioning My Own Siblings
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across Dee, middle sister Junie, and baby-of-the-family Marisol. Each sibling resists for their own reason — grief for grandma, fear of more disappointment, loyalty to mom's rules. Silas wins them over with pancakes and honesty she didn't plan on. Emotional beat: found family recognizing itself.

chapters.title: Theo Marchetti Hums in Thirds
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the qualifier, she meets Theo, whose family has dominated the championship for generations — and whose easy warmth disarms her mid-competition. He offers to trade technique tips; she refuses out of pride, then can't stop thinking about his harmony lines. Emotional beat: attraction as disruption of duty.

chapters.title: Mom Finds Out
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Coming home early from a double shift, Mom discovers the secret rehearsals and explodes — the championship was how she and grandma stopped speaking, and she forbids it. Silas, cornered, says the unsayable: 'You're never here, so I get to decide.' Emotional beat: love against duty, both sides bleeding.

chapters.title: Track Six: What We Don't Say Out Loud
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. With mom frozen out and Silas spiraling, Junie secretly finishes tape six alone and learns grandma wrote it during her own estrangement from Mom — a letter of apology set to music. The siblings play it for Mom without Silas knowing. Emotional beat: inherited wounds, offered balm.

chapters.title: The Night Before Everything
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Finals eve: the oven breaks, the money math doesn't work, and Theo shows up at the door with a borrowed stand mixer and no agenda except her. Silas lets him help — lets anyone help — for the first time. Mom appears in the doorway, apron in hand. Emotional beat: surrender as strength.

chapters.title: The Championship That Matters
chapters.summary: Full-cast POV mosaic. On stage, the Hallorans perform the final tape — grandma's last track, completed with their own voices — while Theo's family watches their dynasty end graciously. Mid-song, the power cuts; the family keeps singing a cappella, and the crowd joins. Emotional beat: visibility chosen, not forced.

chapters.title: Leftovers, Reheated
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, weeks later. The prize money covers rent, not miracles — but Mom took a day shift, Theo is teaching Marisol guitar, and the recipe box now holds blank cards waiting for new tracks. Silas writes the first one herself. Emotional beat: belonging isn't found, it's made — and she's making it.
